item.dc:creator: Sam Sifton
item.media:credit: Stephen Lam/San Francisco Chronicle, via Associated Press
item.media:description: In Naalehu, Hawaii.

item.title: El Niño Is Back. And Worse Than Ever.
item.description: The recurring climate phenomenon is poised this year to enter a new phase known as a super El Niño, exacerbating the effects of climate change.
item.dc:creator: Michael Barbaro, Chico Harlan, Asthaa Chaturvedi, Stella Tan, Adrienne Hurst, Devon Taylor, Marion Lozano, Diane Wong, Pat McCusker and Chris Wood
item.media:credit: Bay Ismoyo/Agence France-Presse — Getty Images
item.media:description: Rocks exposed at the bottom of a river in Tangerang, Indonesia, last month. Falling water levels in the region are due in part to El Niño, which has brought a prolonged dry season and led to extreme drought, threatening food security in parts of Indonesia.

item.title: Hurricane Lala Destroyed a Hawaii Cemetery, Setting Off a Hunt for the Dead
item.description: In the hamlet of Naalehu, the floods of Hurricane Lala opened graves. One mother sought desperately for her son.
item.dc:creator: Meghan Miner Murray and Madaleine Rubin
item.media:credit: Meghan Miner Murray
item.media:description: The storm turned the small cemetery into torrents of mud, bearing the detritus of death.

item.title: Residents on Hawaii’s Big Island Look to Help One Another After Hurricane Lala
item.description: In a remote region of the ravaged Big Island, there were community gas runs, donated turkey stuffing, a makeshift emergency broadcast and even a helicopter.
item.dc:creator: Orlando Mayorquín
item.media:credit: Ronit Fahl for The New York Times
item.media:description: Brandy Field, from Ka’u Radio, helps to set up internet access in Ocean View, Hawaii, on Monday after Hurricane Lala. The storm knocked out power to thousands on the Big Island.

item.title: What We Know About Damage From Hurricane Lala in Hawaii
item.description: The storm narrowly missed land, but its outer bands left the Big Island with power outages, road closures and flooded homes. At least three people have died in the storm.
item.dc:creator: Christina Morales and Judson Jones
item.media:credit: Bruce Omori for The New York Times
item.media:description: Damage from the storm in Mountain View on the Big Island of Hawaii.

item.title: American Hiker Dies After Lightning Strike on Mount Etna in Italy
item.description: Rescuers found a 29-year-old man in serious condition on the volcano’s eastern slope on Sunday. He was later pronounced dead at a hospital in Catania.
item.dc:creator: Leo Sands and Josephine de La Bruyère
item.media:credit: Salvatore Allegra/Associated Press
item.media:description: Volcanic activity at Mount Etna as seen from Mareneve near Catania in Italy last week. Italian authorities say a 29-year-old American hiker was killed by lightning while hiking on Europe’s most active volcano.

item.title: Watch Out for El Niño
item.description: We explain the climate phenomenon.
item.dc:creator: Chico Harlan
item.media:credit: Ritesh Shukla/Getty Images
item.media:description: Collecting water from a well in a drought-afflicted village in India.

item.title: Hurricane Lala Cuts Off Hawaii Town With Region’s Only Hospital
item.description: Residents of Pahala were stranded after parts of a key highway collapsed under heavy rain. All roads leading to the town and its hospital, on the southern end of the Big Island, are now blocked.
item.dc:creator: Francesca Regalado
item.media:credit: Jill K. Briggs/Agence France-Presse — Getty Images
item.media:description: Hawaii Department of Transportation workers inspect road damage caused by Hurricane Lala in Pahala on Sunday.

item.title: Hurricane Lala Batters Hilo, Hawaii, Destroying Homes and Leaving Thousands Without Power
item.description: The city on the eastern side of the island of Hawaii flooded on Saturday night, and powerful winds toppled branches onto homes and power lines.
item.dc:creator: Orlando Mayorquín
item.media:credit: Bruce Omori for The New York Times
item.media:description: Soccer fields in Hilo flooded as heavy rains from Hurricane Lala inundated parts of the island of Hawaii on Saturday.

item.title: Indiana Prepares for More Rain After Days of Deadly Storms
item.description: Since last week, hazardous weather has caused seven deaths, forced people from their homes and required some to be rescued by boat. The region was at risk for more flooding on Sunday.
item.dc:creator: Bernard Mokam
item.media:credit: Michelle Pemberton/USA Today Network, via Reuters
item.media:description: Evacuation efforts in Indianapolis on Saturday.

item.title: Lala Damages Utility Lines in Hawaii, Leaving Thousands Without Power
item.description: Tropical Storm Lala damaged 16 transmission lines and many towers on Hawaii’s Big Island, the state’s main utility said.
item.dc:creator: Ivan Penn
item.media:credit: Bruce Omori for The New York Times
item.media:description: A crew dealing with a damaged utility pole in Hilo, Hawaii, on Saturday. Hawaiian Electric, the state’s primary electric utility, said its customers faced days without power because of the extent of the damage.

item.title: As Lala Lashes Hawaii, the Atlantic Hurricane Season Remains Calm. So Far.
item.description: An El Niño weather pattern is expected to limit activity into the fall, providing a stabilizing force.
item.dc:creator: Judson Jones
item.media:credit: Brandon Bell/Getty Images
item.media:description: Tropical Storm Arthur made landfall in Freeport, Texas, in June, flooding neighborhoods and becoming the first named tropical storm of the 2026 Atlantic hurricane season.

item.title: Aircraft That Typically Track Atlantic Storms Are Flying Into Lala
item.description: With Atlantic activity down this season, rare Pacific missions are being undertaken to better understand the storm skirting Hawaii.
item.dc:creator: Judson Jones
item.media:credit: Zack Wittman for The New York Times
item.media:description: NOAA’s Hurricane Hunter flight team piloted a plane through Tropical Storm Helene in 2024.

item.dc:creator: Jin Yu Young
item.media:credit: Sai Aung Main/Agence France-Presse — Getty Images
item.media:description: The emergency department of Yangon General Hospital on Friday.

item.title: Hurricane Lala Threatens Hawaii Farms Still Recovering From March Floods
item.description: Hawaii imports most of its food, but Lala could still deal a significant blow to state agriculture. March storms caused at least $50 million in damages to crops, livestock and equipment.
item.dc:creator: Pooja Salhotra
item.media:credit: Stephen Lam/San Francisco Chronicle, via Associated Press
item.media:description: An aerial view of a flooded farm after storms in Haleiwa, Oahu, in March.

item.title: Shelters Open as Lala Advances Toward Hawaii
item.description: A mix of tourists and locals began gathering at a high school on Saturday morning.
item.dc:creator: Orlando Mayorquín and Ishani Desai
item.media:credit: Bruce Omori for The New York Times
item.media:description: Social workers speaking with a person in Hilo, Hawaii, on Friday.

item.title: Some Daring Surfers Seek Waves as Hurricane Lala Approaches
item.description: “We have time, so why don’t we enjoy it?” one beachgoer said as the storm made its way across the Pacific.
item.dc:creator: Meghan Miner Murray and Pooja Salhotra
item.media:credit: Meghan Miner Murray for The New York Times
item.media:description: Surfers at Magic Sands in Kailua-Kona, Hawaii, on Saturday morning even as Hurricane Lala approached the Big Island.

item.title: Lala Heads for a State With Older Housing Stock
item.description: Experts warned that many houses on the Big Island weren’t built for hurricane-force wind and rain.
item.dc:creator: Aimee Ortiz
item.media:credit: Allan Baxter/Getty Images
item.media:description: Houses at the water’s edge of the Big Island of Hawaii. The median age of a house on the island is 37 years old, and older homes will be more vulnerable to heavy winds and rain.

item.title: Hawaii Braces for Lala After Earlier Flooding
item.description: The state experienced some of its worst flooding in decades during storms earlier this year, the governor said.
item.dc:creator: Sejal Govindarao
item.media:credit: Gabriela Bhaskar/The New York Times
item.media:description: Slow-moving storms in March caused heavy flooding across Hawaii, hitting Oahu, the state’s most populous island, particularly hard.

item.title: How Did This Hurricane Get the Name Lala?
item.description: Names come from a list developed by a meteorological organization. They can help people pay attention, an official with the National Hurricane Center said.
item.dc:creator: Amy Graff
item.media:credit: Bruce Omori for The New York Times
item.media:description: Maile Madrona, who works at a store in downtown Hilo, Hawaii, placed sandbags outside the shop on Friday.

item.title: The Last Hurricane to Hit Hawaii Became a Movie Star
item.description: Hurricane Iniki devastated Kauai, causing at least seven deaths and $1.8 billion in damage. It also got a cameo in a Spielberg movie.
item.dc:creator: Amy Graff and Pooja Salhotra
item.media:credit: Reed Saxon/Associated Press
item.media:description: Rubble left behind after Hurricane Iniki battered the island of Kauai in 1992.

item.title: An Island Used to Storms Readies for One of the Strongest in Decades
item.description: Storms regularly sweep across Hawaii, but actual hurricanes are rare. As Lala approached, propane, ice and Oreos were among the priorities.
item.dc:creator: Orlando Mayorquín and Pooja Salhotra
item.media:credit: Bruce Omori for The New York Times
item.media:description: Maile Madrona placing sandbags at the base of their entrance of Aloha Grown, a local shop in downtown Hilo, Hawaii, on Friday.

item.title: Travelers Hunker Down as Hurricane Lala Approaches Hawaii’s Big Island
item.description: The storm has prompted some travelers to leave their hotels early, while others are waiting out the wind and rain.
item.dc:creator: Ryley Ober
item.media:credit: Kevin Carter/Getty Images
item.media:description: Many flights to and from the Big Island of Hawaii have been canceled as airlines prepare for Hurricane Lala.

item.title: N.Y.C. Congestion Pricing Has Little Effect on Air Quality, Study Finds
item.description: The report from New York City’s Health Department found that pollution improved slightly in Manhattan and did not worsen in other boroughs.
item.dc:creator: Hilary Howard
item.media:credit: Karsten Moran for The New York Times
item.media:description: Congestion pricing, which began in 2025, charges most drivers up to $9 to enter Manhattan below 60th Street during peak traffic hours.

item.title: Heat Deaths in a ‘Cold’ Country Are a Warning to the Rest of Europe
item.description: A June heat wave in Belgium and neighboring countries exposed a lethal lack of readiness. That’s a risk as another wave hits Europe.
item.dc:creator: Jeanna Smialek and Koba Ryckewaert
item.media:credit: Ksenia Kuleshova for The New York Times
item.media:description: Treating a 77-year-old woman for heat-related illness last month at MontLégia hospital in the Belgian city of Liège.

item.title: Hawaiian Electric Warns That Power Outages Could Last for Days
item.description: Strong winds from Tropical Storm Lala, which will likely become a hurricane while approaching Hawaii, are expected to topple trees and down power lines.
item.dc:creator: Ivan Penn
item.media:credit: Rick Bowmer/Associated Press
item.media:description: Linemen working on poles in 2023 after wildfires in Hawaii. The state’s largest power company advised residents ahead of Lala.
